chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar from al-Salih ibn al-Sandiy from Ibn Mahbub from al-'Ali from al-Mismaa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding

a man who forgot to shave or trim [his hair/nails] until he departed [for Hajj]. He [the Imam] said: He shaves if he remembers while on the road or wherever he is. I asked him: Does the Muhrim wear the ring? He said: He does not wear it for adornment.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: the person in the state of Ihram

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who forgets to trim their hair before entering Ihram, and can they wear a ring?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *al-Istibsar*, this hadith clarifies the ruling for a pilgrim who forgets to trim hair or nails before entering Ihram, establishing that they must shave or trim immediately upon remembering, regardless of their location. It further distinguishes the permissibility of wearing a ring while in Ihram, prohibiting it only if worn for adornment (Zinah), thereby highlighting the principle that minor accessories are permissible unless their primary purpose is beautification.
